title: Developing A Framework to Support Human Evaluation of Bias in Generated Free Response Text

bias_targets.methodology: Generating free-text responses to ambiguous and disambiguated context templates from the BBQ benchmark and evaluating equivalence under counterfactual name substitution (name reversal).
Evaluating free-text LLM responses for equivalence after substituting names and descriptors associated with disability status using adapted BBQ benchmark templates.
Applying counterfactual name substitution (e.g., swapping 'man' and 'woman') in free-response prompts and analyzing variations or lack of equivalence in the model's text generation.
Comparing generated free-text responses for equivalence when swapping names or descriptors associated with different nationalities in prompt templates.
Generating and comparing free-response texts from the model using counterfactual descriptor substitution related to physical appearance.
Evaluating free-text responses to BBQ templates for bias by reversing names or descriptors associated with different racial and ethnic groups and checking for response parity.
Using name and descriptor reversal in free-response prompt templates to detect disparate predictions or reasoning related to socioeconomic status.
Analyzing deviations and stereotyping in free-text LLM responses when swapping religious group identifiers (e.g., Hindu vs. Catholic) in context templates.
Testing the equivalence and parity of free-text reasoning under name and descriptor reversal for sexual orientation contexts.
